blocks.x: The working definition of Digital Workforce & Multi-Agent Orchestration at Dataq Software: scope we sign, the cadence you can plan around, platform evidence generated in-flight, and outcomes measured against your baseline.

Scaling from five agents to five hundred breaks ad-hoc patterns: conflicts over shared systems, duplicated work, no cost accountability, no way to know which agent did what. We build the orchestration layer that treats agents as a managed workforce — role definitions, task queues and bidding, shared-memory contracts, per-team budgets, kill switches, and a control tower showing fleet health, throughput and cost per completed task.

The orchestration core runs on durable execution (Temporal-class runtimes) with idempotent task semantics, priority lanes for SLA-bound work, and a policy engine that routes high-risk actions to approval workflows. Fleet upgrades are staged like software releases: shadow mode, canary cohorts, and automatic rollback on eval regression.

The rhythm is fixed on purpose: progress becomes visible from week one, not after the first steering meeting. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
